name: Harold Mellor
bio: Wealthy English expatriate, and Wilde's host, patron and travelling companion through the exile years 1898-1900. Per the editors of the Complete Letters, 'the neurotic son of a Bolton cotton spinner', left wealthy by his father's death in 1893, who 'spent most of the rest of his life abroad, finally committing suicide in his villa at Cannes'; his aunt Ursula Mellor married the Liberal MP Jacob Bright. Wilde met him at Napoule at Christmas 1898 and stayed at his villa at Gland, Vaud, in March-April 1899 and again in July-August 1900; Mellor also funded Wilde's journey to Italy in 1900 'to the extent of £50'. Wilde recorded Mellor's own queer life in two letters: that he had been 'sent away from Harrow at the age of fourteen for being loved by the captain of the cricket eleven', and that he 'has Greek loves, and is rather ashamed of them'. The Italian servant Eolo travelled with him from at least 1898 until 1900.
bio_sources: Life-dates, family, wealth, expatriation and manner of death: 'Harold Mellor (1868-1925) was the neurotic son of a Bolton cotton spinner. His father died in 1893, leaving him wealthy, and he spent most of the rest of his life abroad, finally committing suicide in his villa at Cannes. His aunt Ursula Mellor married Jacob Bright (1821-99), brother of John Bright and Liberal MP for Manchester 1867-95 with two short intervals.' - Holland & Hart-Davis, editors' footnote, Complete Letters (2000), p. 1112n (repo PDF 1158, printed folio confirmed on rendered page image, 2026-08-03).

The meeting: 'A nice fellow called Harold Mellor, who is staying at Cannes, comes over constantly to see me. He is a nephew of Mrs Jacob Bright's.' - Wilde to Robert Ross, [27 December 1898], Napoule; p. 1112 (repo PDF 1158, folio confirmed, rendered 2026-08-03).

Harrow: 'a charming fellow called Harold Mellor (sent away from Harrow at the age of fourteen for being loved by the captain of the cricket eleven) who is staying with his mother near Cannes, and comes over on his bicycle to breakfast every morning' - Wilde to Robert Ross, 2 January 1899, Napoule; p. 1116 (repo PDF 1162, folio confirmed, rendered 2026-08-03).

'Greek loves' and the patronage frame: 'I don't like Mellor: he is a silent, dull person, cautious, and economical … has Greek loves, and is rather ashamed of them: has heaps of money, and lives in terror of poverty: so I regard it as a sort of Swiss pension, where there is no weekly bill.' - Wilde to Reginald Turner, [postmark 20 March 1899], Gland; p. 1132 (repo PDF 1178, folio confirmed, rendered 2026-08-03).

The 1900 Italy money: 'Mellor, with whom I am now friends (below zero of course) has invited me to go to Italy to the extent of £50!' - Wilde to Robert Ross, [late March 1900], Paris; p. 1177 (repo PDF 1223, folio confirmed, rendered 2026-08-03).

The last visit and Mellor's own surviving letter: 'I have been with Harold Mellor at Gland: he is almost as neurasthenic as I am' - Wilde to Ross, [August 1900]; and editors' footnote 1 on the same page: 'A surviving letter from Mellor to Wilde (MS Clark), written from Gland and dated 21 July 1900, runs: "Am much distressed about your illness . . . I hope to be able to receive you on Monday 30 [July]."' - p. 1194 (repo PDF 1240, folio confirmed, rendered 2026-08-03).
bio_note: Dates: the editors' footnote gives the death year only inside the life-dates (1868-1925); it does not date the suicide separately, and the place is 'his villa at Cannes'. Wilde's own estimate of Mellor's age - 'He is about twenty-six, but looks younger' (2 January 1899) - is wrong against the editors' 1868 birth-year, which would make him 30; recorded as Wilde's impression, not as a fact. Register: the friendly words are the first-impression ones of December 1898 and January 1899; from printed 1129 onward Wilde's private register toward Mellor is hostile ('very lamentable', 'this loathsome place', 'Gland, which has become intolerable', 'this dreadful place' - three correspondents in one week, March 1899, all p. 1137, repo PDF 1183, folio confirmed). Sensitive-content register (README): Mellor's age at the Harrow expulsion is fourteen, as the letter states it, no gloss. NULL FINDING - no mellor--wilde relationship file exists: the record in the pages read is companionship, hospitality and patronage in both directions, with no romantic or sexual content and no third-party or editorial characterization of the pair as anything but host and guest. Mellor's own documented queerness is a fact about Mellor and is not evidence about the pair. Cross-thread note: p. 1194 carries Wilde's use of 'neurasthenia' as a diagnosis for himself and for Mellor - relevant to the separate sexual-neurasthenia thread, though nothing there ties the term to sexual aetiology. Full passages, the null-finding table and the unread-page pointers in dossiers/EXILE-COMPANIONS_dossier.md (M1-M9).
